# Registered: C6 mechanism at scale — does the readout/anchor dissociation hold at 7B (v1)

**Filed:** 2026-08-11, **before any C6 estimand has been computed.**
**Status at filing:** the six C6 cells are being generated by `scripts/c6_cells_chain.sh`
(log `logs/c6_cells_chain.log`). One cell (`r19_base7b`) has finalized; the remaining five
are queued or in flight. No C6 readout script has been run; no per-role accuracy, no
arm-minus-base difference, and no interval exists for any cell. The single exception —
one shard-level, role-mixed metrics line seen during authoring — is disclosed in the
Deviations Log below rather than left unrecorded.

Analysis git HEAD at filing: `ee7fd256f321c39bfd5f7ed47614093fdb337bbd`.

## 1. What is being tested, and why

Two established results run along two different axes. C6 joins them.

**Axis 1 — the mechanism (fixed scale, varied recipe).** At 3B, outcome-reward RLVR moves
the **oracle-localized readout** while leaving the **primary visual anchor** flat, and F3 →
F8 → Gate 1 established that this dissociation is *recipe-independent*: all four Mini-A5
recipes (standard GRPO, paired-data member, necessity, CP/IGPO) move the readout control
+0.15–0.23 lenient while no axis buys held-out content on the primary anchor under any
contrast or any role (`reports/mini_a5_gate1_endpoint_readout_v1.json`,
`docs/registered_mini_a5_endpoint_readout_v1.md`, `docs/registered_gate1_four_arm_v1.md`).

**Axis 2 — scale (fixed recipe, varied model).** R4/C5 held the seed-1 geo3k recipe fixed
and changed only the model to 7B. The blind-attainable share of the gain **grows** with
scale: crossed TrainShare for A2-gray 0.7785 [0.6418, 0.9214] canonical / 0.8402 [0.7457,
0.9456] strict at 7B against a 3B pooled 0.487 [0.383, 0.588], intervals disjoint
(`reports/c5_r4_readout_v1.json`, `docs/registered_c5_7b_access_pair_v1.md`). That is a
cross-scale *descriptive* contrast, so labelled there and so labelled here.

**C6's question, and only this question:** does the readout/anchor dissociation established
at 3B still hold when the trained model is 7B? Nothing else is at issue. C6 does not
re-decide Gate 1, does not re-decide R4, and computes no cross-scale statistic.

The instrument reports. It does not editorialize, does not rank the branches by
desirability, and does not convert a descriptive outcome into a claim.

## 4. The three task roles — never aggregated (I13)

Both instruments carry the same three template ids in the same 600/300/300 composition
(verified on both manifests, 2026-08-11):

| template_id | n pairs | role | how it is read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `coordinate_register_twenty_point_x_v02` | 600 | **primary visual anchor** (search + binding + read) | the anchor half of the dissociation |
| `header_cued_table_code_v02` | 300 | saturated positive control / **retention canary** | read only in its own retention role; a DROP signals damage |
| `starred_series_value_nine_v07` | 300 | **oracle-localized readout control** | the readout half of the dissociation |

No number that mixes these three roles is an endpoint. Any pooled quantity the readout
emits appears only under a key explicitly labelled `NOT_AN_ENDPOINT` (the convention of
`reports/mini_a5_gate1_endpoint_readout_v1.json`). Shard-level metrics are role-mixed by
construction (the launcher shards the manifest across four GPUs without regard to
template; the observed composition of R19 shard 0 is 162/76/62) and are therefore **never**
an estimand at any point in this registration.

## 5. Cells — six, and how they are bound

Three models × two instruments, all under `image_mode: real`, greedy decoding
(`temperature 0.0`, `n 1`, `top_p 1.0`), `max_new_tokens 32`, `seed 0`, prompt contract
`answer-tags-v1` / `7ac39f53a2a824490fc5ee22671a888d2d79d55e1d8351919006d7d71c7a8f3f`,
four shards on an12 GPUs 0–3.

| Cell | Model | Instrument |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `r19_base7b` | frozen 7B base | R19 |
| `r19_a1real` | A1-real | R19 |
| `r19_a2gray` | A2-gray | R19 |
| `r20_base7b` | frozen 7B base | R20 |
| `r20_a1real` | A1-real | R20 |
| `r20_a2gray` | A2-gray | R20 |

**Cells are bound by manifest content, not by directory name.** The generating chain was
restarted during generation and its two versions use different run-directory naming
(`experiments/runs/c6_r19_7b_base_real_an12_20260811T120648Z` from the first, and the
`experiments/runs/c6_{r19,r20}_{base7b,a1real,a2gray}_an12_<TS>` form from the second, e.g.
`experiments/runs/c6_r19_a1real_an12_20260811T122252Z`). Directory names are therefore
**not** a registered identifier. A cell qualifies for a slot in the table above iff its
`run_manifest.json` carries the registered `model_revision` for that row and the registered
`data_manifest_hash` for that column, together with the full contract fields checked in §8.
The chain's pointer files `logs/c6_cells/<label>` record which run directory was banked for
each label; the readout resolves cells through those pointers and then re-verifies every
binding field from the manifest itself. A pointer that does not verify is a hard failure,
not a fallback to name matching. The resolved run directories and their
`run_manifest.json` sha256 are recorded in the readout's `inputs_sha256` block.

## 6. The 7B base is re-run deliberately — and why

7B base FlipTrack cells already exist from 2026-07-10/11
(`experiments/runs/fliptrack_v02r19_packaged_qwen25vl7b_real_an12_20260710T143628Z` and the
R20 twin of 2026-07-11). **They are not used, and they are not comparable.** Their rows
predate the canonical scoring contract: the row schema carries no `contract_valid`, no
`parser_version`, and no `prompt_contract_id` (verified 2026-08-11 by field inspection —
all three keys absent), so the strict channel was produced by a pre-canonical parser and is
near-degenerate against the lenient one (it differs on 3 of 1,200 pairs). The current
contract's strict channel is a genuinely different measurement — at 3B it separates from
lenient by tens of points on the canary role — and an arm-minus-base difference formed
across the two schemas would attribute a *parser change* to *training*.

Re-running the base under the current contract costs one inference pass and removes the
confound entirely. It is a re-run for comparability, not a second look at a result: no
value from the 2026-07-10/11 base cells enters any C6 estimand, and the readout refuses any
cell whose rows lack the contract fields (§8, check 6), which excludes them by construction
rather than by convention.

## 7. Estimands

**Comparison engine, reused unchanged:**
`scripts/compare_fliptrack_runs.py::compare_rows(left_rows, right_rows, left_label,
right_label, *, seed=20260712, bootstrap_draws=2000)`, with
`src.eval.fliptrack_metrics.aggregate_pair_metrics_by_template` for per-role cell levels.
Pair-level success is `src.eval.fliptrack_metrics.pair_score` (both members correct).
`scripts/build_mini_a5_gate1_endpoint_readout.py` is **not** reused: its `ARM_ORDER`,
`ARM_LABELS` and `ARM_CHECKPOINT_TOKENS` are hard-coded to the Mini-A5 arms and its
`--base-report` is the 3B base.

**Orientation.** `compare_rows` returns `pair_accuracy_delta = right − left`. Every C6
contrast is therefore called with **`left` = the 7B base cell** and **`right` = the arm
cell**, so every registered delta is *arm minus base*. This orientation is fixed here and
is asserted by the readout, not chosen at analysis time.

**The registered contrasts** — four, each read at three roles under two contracts
(4 × 3 × 2 = 24 registered numbers):

| id | left (base) | right (arm) | instrument |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `c6_1_a1real_minus_base_r19` | `r19_base7b` | `r19_a1real` | R19 |
| `c6_2_a2gray_minus_base_r19` | `r19_base7b` | `r19_a2gray` | R19 |
| `c6_3_a1real_minus_base_r20` | `r20_base7b` | `r20_a1real` | R20 (replication) |
| `c6_4_a2gray_minus_base_r20` | `r20_base7b` | `r20_a2gray` | R20 (replication) |

For each contrast, at each of the three `template_id` roles, under **both** contracts:

- lenient: `pair_accuracy_delta`, `pair_accuracy_delta_ci95_low`,
  `pair_accuracy_delta_ci95_high`, and the exact two-sided McNemar `mcnemar`;
- contract-strict: `strict_pair_accuracy_delta`, `strict_pair_accuracy_delta_ci95_low`,
  `strict_pair_accuracy_delta_ci95_high`, and `strict_mcnemar`.

Cell levels (`left_pair_accuracy`, `right_pair_accuracy` and their strict twins, per role,
per cell) are reported alongside as descriptive levels. They are not endpoints.

**Both contracts are reported and never merged (I7).** Neither is privileged. If they
disagree, the disagreement is the result and is stated as the result.

**Interval procedure — pinned to the values `compare_rows` uses.** Paired item bootstrap,
unit = `pair_id`, both sides resampled on the same pair indices per replicate, percentile
95% (2.5 / 97.5), **2,000 draws**, **base seed 20260712** — the defaults in the
`compare_rows` signature, adopted deliberately rather than overridden. The engine's seed
derivation, restated so it is auditable: pooled lenient `seed`, pooled strict `seed + 1`;
for the k-th template in sorted order, lenient `seed + 100 + 10k`, strict `+ 1`. With
`seed = 20260712` and the three roles in sorted order that is

| role (sorted order) | lenient seed | strict seed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `coordinate_register_twenty_point_x_v02` (k=0) | 20260812 | 20260813 |
| `header_cued_table_code_v02` (k=1) | 20260822 | 20260823 |
| `starred_series_value_nine_v07` (k=2) | 20260832 | 20260833 |

Intervals quantify **evaluation uncertainty on a fixed pair set**. They do not estimate
run-to-run RL variance. Each arm is one run.

**Pooled-across-roles values.** `compare_rows` also returns pooled top-level deltas (seeds
20260712 / 20260713). Under I13 these are not endpoints; they are emitted only under a key
labelled `NOT_AN_ENDPOINT` and are never read as a C6 result.

**Decision rule.** **MOVED** iff the 95% paired-bootstrap CI excludes zero in the positive
direction. A positive point estimate whose interval contains zero is **NOT MOVED** — not
"a trend". **MOVED_NEGATIVE_DIRECTION** iff the CI lies entirely below zero. Identical to
the Gate-1 rule (`reports/mini_a5_gate1_endpoint_readout_v1.json` → `instrument`).

**One-seed tag.** Every emitted number carries
`seed_tag: "one seed (data.seed 1; single 7B training pair)"`. No between-seed variance
claim is made anywhere in C6.

**Cross-scale.** Any comparison to the 3B Mini-A5 / Gate-1 numbers is **descriptive** and
carried as a labelled string, exactly as R4 carried its 3B anchor. **No cross-scale
statistic is computed** — no cross-scale difference, ratio, interval or test.

## 8. The pre-committed reading — stated before any value is seen

Read on the **A1-real** contrast (`c6_1` on R19, replicated by `c6_3` on R20), from the two
halves of the dissociation: the **anchor** = `coordinate_register_twenty_point_x_v02`, the
**readout** = `starred_series_value_nine_v07`. The same four branches are also applied to
the A2-gray contrast (`c6_2`, `c6_4`) and reported there under the blind-trained-arm label
of §2.

- **(a) readout MOVED, anchor NOT MOVED** → **the dissociation is scale-independent.**
  Reported as the central C6 result: outcome-reward RLVR at 7B moves the oracle-localized
  readout while leaving the primary visual anchor flat, as it does at 3B across four
  recipes.
- **(b) readout MOVED and anchor MOVED** → **a scale-dependent mechanism.** Reported as
  such: at 7B the same recipe reaches the primary anchor, which the 3B recipes did not.
  This is a finding about scale, and it is reported without being softened into (a).
- **(c) neither MOVED** → reported **descriptively as 7B recipe transfer**: the C5 recipe
  transferred to 7B on its own training distribution (R4) without moving either FlipTrack
  layer. No dissociation claim is made in either direction from this branch.
- **(d) anchor MOVED, readout NOT MOVED** → the remaining cell of the 2×2. It is not
  anticipated by any prior result and no interpretation is pre-committed for it; it is
  reported descriptively, with the raw numbers, and explicitly flagged as an unregistered
  outcome. Naming it here prevents it from being quietly folded into (a) or (b).

**In every branch, the canary is read in its own retention role.**
`header_cued_table_code_v02` is a saturated positive control: it never contributes to the
anchor/readout branch decision and is never netted against either. Its reading is
independent and has its own consequence — **MOVED_NEGATIVE_DIRECTION on the canary is a
damage signal** and is reported as damage, under whichever branch (a)–(d) fired for the
other two roles. A branch (a) accompanied by canary damage is reported as "(a) with canary
damage", not as (a).

**Contract disagreement (I7).** The branch is evaluated separately under lenient and under
contract-strict. If the two contracts fire different branches, **both branches are
reported**, the disagreement is named as the result, and neither contract is chosen as the
tie-breaker. No merged or averaged contract exists.

**R20 is a replication, not a vote.** Its branch reading is reported next to R19's. If the
two instruments fire different branches, that is reported as a replication failure of the
branch on the twin — it is not resolved by pooling, averaging, or majority.

## 9. Acceptance checks the readout must enforce

The readout emits **no estimand** unless all of the following pass. Each is a hard refusal,
not a warning.

1. **Six cells bound.** All six slots of §5 resolve to exactly one run directory each, via
   `logs/c6_cells/<label>`, with no slot filled twice and no directory serving two slots.
2. **Model identity.** Each cell's `run_manifest.json` `model_revision` resolves to the
   registered path for its row in §2 (base / A1-real / A2-gray).
3. **Manifest hash pins.** Each cell's `data_manifest` equals the registered path for its
   column and its `data_manifest_hash` equals the registered sha256 (`e1dde984…` for R19,
   `20222e60…` for R20); the on-disk manifest is re-hashed at readout time and must match
   the same value.
4. **Complete run manifests.** `status == "complete"`, `expected_shards == 4` with four
   shard files and four shard metrics present, and `performance_values_opened == false` at
   generation time.
5. **Locked evaluation contract, identical across all six cells.**
   `prompt_contract_id == "answer-tags-v1"`,
   `prompt_contract_sha256 == "7ac39f53a2a824490fc5ee22671a888d2d79d55e1d8351919006d7d71c7a8f3f"`,
   `decoding == {n: 1, temperature: 0.0, top_p: 1.0}`, `max_new_tokens == 32`,
   `image_mode == "real"`, `seed == 0`. Base and arms are evaluated identically (I7).
6. **Canonical contract fields present on every row.** Every row carries `contract_valid`,
   `parser_version == "canonical-v2"` and `prompt_contract_id == "answer-tags-v1"`. This is
   the check that structurally excludes the 2026-07-10/11 base cells of §6.
7. **Both contracts present.** Every row carries both `pair_correct` and
   `strict_pair_correct`; both channels are computed for every cell and every role; no
   emitted key merges or averages them.
8. **Item-set identity across the three models, per instrument.** For R19, the `pair_id`
   sets of `r19_base7b`, `r19_a1real` and `r19_a2gray` are pairwise **and three-way**
   identical; likewise for R20. `template_id` per `pair_id` is identical across the three
   models. Duplicate `pair_id` within any cell is a refusal.
9. **Instrument separation.** The R19 and R20 `pair_id` sets are disjoint (expected
   intersection 0). No estimand, and no intermediate structure, combines rows from the two
   instruments.
10. **Per-role `n_pairs`.** For R19 exactly
    `coordinate_register_twenty_point_x_v02 = 600`, `header_cued_table_code_v02 = 300`,
    `starred_series_value_nine_v07 = 300`, total 1,200. The same 600/300/300 composition is
    checked for R20 and recorded. Any deviation is a refusal, not a rescaling.
11. **Bootstrap parameters as registered.** The values actually passed to `compare_rows` are
    asserted equal to `bootstrap_draws == 2000` and `seed == 20260712`, and the derived
    per-role seeds of §7 are recorded in the report.
12. **Orientation.** Every contrast is asserted to have been called with the base cell as
    `left` and the arm cell as `right`.
13. **I13 enforcement.** No pooled-across-roles quantity appears except under a key whose
    name contains `NOT_AN_ENDPOINT`. No shard-level quantity appears at all.
14. **One-seed tagging (I15 + seed scope).** `schema_version` is carried at top level and
    every emitted number carries the one-seed `seed_tag` of §7.
15. **Cross-scale discipline.** No cross-scale statistic is computed; 3B anchors appear only
    as labelled descriptive strings.
16. **Determinism and immutability.** Two invocations at the registered seed produce
    byte-identical output; the readout refuses to overwrite an existing report.

**Registered artifacts.** `scripts/build_c6_mechanism_at_scale_readout.py` →
`reports/c6_mechanism_at_scale_v1.json` (+ `.md`), `schema_version`
`blind-gains.c6-mechanism-at-scale-readout.v1`, with an `inputs_sha256` block covering every
consumed shard file and `run_manifest.json`.

**I10 — adversarial fixtures pass BEFORE the instrument touches real cells.**
`tests/test_build_c6_mechanism_at_scale_readout_fixture.py` must exist and pass, on
synthetic cells only, before the readout is pointed at any C6 run directory. It must
include, at minimum: planted per-role values recovered exactly under both contracts;
item-set mismatch between models refused; a `pair_id` present in two models but not the
third refused; manifest-hash mismatch refused; missing or `status != complete` run manifest
refused; wrong `model_revision` for a slot refused; rows lacking `contract_valid` /
`parser_version` (the 2026-07-10 schema) refused; per-role `n_pairs` off the registered
600/300/300 refused; R19/R20 rows combined refused; a pooled endpoint emitted without the
`NOT_AN_ENDPOINT` label refused; reversed orientation refused; two invocations
byte-identical; refusal to overwrite an existing report.

## 10. Scope, and what C6 cannot say

- **One seed, one 7B training pair.** Every number is a one-seed number. C6 makes no
  between-seed variance claim and cannot distinguish a scale effect from a single-run
  draw. That limit is a property of the C5 design (two arms, `data.seed 1`), not something
  C6 can repair by analysis.
- **Two arms, not four.** The 3B dissociation was established across four recipes; the 7B
  side has one real-image arm and one blind arm. C6 tests whether the dissociation *holds*
  at 7B for the transferred recipe. It does not establish recipe-independence at 7B.
- **Descriptive cross-scale only.** Nothing in C6 licenses a tested claim that the
  dissociation is stronger, weaker, or equal at 7B versus 3B.
- **No re-decision.** Gate 1 and R4 stand as filed. C6 neither confirms nor overturns them.

## 11. Sealed

No C6 estimand is computed until this document is merged. The pre-committed reading of §8
is in force from the moment of filing and is not amended after any value is seen. R19 and
R20 are never modified, regenerated, or trained on (I11).
